newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-METS BEAT CARDS IN NINTH ON TWO PINCH-HIT HOMERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-METS BEAT CARDS IN NINTH ON TWO PINCH-HIT HOMERS.

text.p: For one day, at least, Butch Huskey was content to be a pinch-hitter.

Huskey followed Carl Everett's two-run homer in the ninth inning with a solo shot of his own to rally the New York Mets to a 6-4 victory over the St Louis Cardinals Sunday, pushing them over the .500 mark for the first time this season.

Carlos Baerga led off the ninth with a single and was forced at second by Alex Ochoa. Everett hit for Manny Alexander and drove a 2-2 pitch from Dennis Eckersley (0-2) over the centre-field wall to erase a 4-3 deficit.

"I got a fastball down the middle at the belt," said Everett. "You can't let those kind of offerings go. I knew that Eckersley would want to get ahead of me, and when he threw a ball, it was my at-bat. I won the battle."
Huskey then hit for reliever Cory Lidle (1-0) and hit a solo shot over the right-field fence for his sixth homer.
The last time the Mets had back-to-back pinch homers was May 4, 1991, when Mackey Sasser and Mark Carreon did it. New York (19-18) has three pinch homers in its last five games.
"I would settle for this role if the result was guaranteed," joked Huskey, who has hit two straight pinch homers.
"Now that we are over .500, our concern has to be playing one game at a time. We can't think that this game made the season. We have plenty of games to play."
Lidle struck out two in a scoreless eighth for his first major-league win. John Franco got his 10th save.
In Pittsburgh, John Smoltz allowed five hits over seven innings and Andruw Jones had three hits and two RBI as the Atlanta Braves defeated the Pirates 8-2.

Smoltz (4-3), the 1996 Cy Young Award winner, allowed two runs, walked two and struck out five. Since allowing a career-high 14 hits in a loss at Colorado on April 20, he has lasted at least seven innings in four straight starts, going 2-0.
Javy Lopez and Jeff Blauser homered for the Braves. Blauser's shot was his second homer in as many games.

At Florida, Alex Fernandez pitched effectively for six innings, delivered a bases-loaded double in a three-run first and helped himself with the glove to lead the Marlins to their third win in four games, 6-3 over the Houston Astros.

Fernandez (3-3) allowed three runs and six hits with three walks and five strikeouts. The right-hander, who spent his first seven years in the American League, also went 1-for-2 with his first two career RBI, raising his batting average to .294.
Fernandez got himself in trouble in the sixth by issuing two two-out walks but speared Sean Berry's comebacker for the final out. Berry had a two-run double for Houston.
In San Francisco, Mark Gardner won his fourth straight decision and the Giants used a season-high five runs in the third inning to rally past the Chicago Cubs 11-5.

Gardner (4-1) allowed four runs and seven hits, walking two and striking out four over 5 1/3 innings. Four relievers finished up, including Doug Henry, who pitched the final 2 1/3 innings for his first save since last August.

J.T. Snow, who played for the Angels last season, hit his first National League homer and drove in three RBI for the Giants. Barry Bonds, who sat out with the flu Saturday, broke out of a 1-for-16 slump with two hits, including a two-run homer that got the Giants on the board in the first inning.

In Los Angeles, Darrin Fletcher, Vladimir Guerrero and Henry Rodriguez all had two-out RBI singles in the 10th inning as the Montreal Expos rallied past the Dodgers 6-3, salvaging the final game of their three-game series.

The Expos forced extra innings in the ninth when Doug Strange hit a full-count offering from Los Angeles closer Todd Worrell that barely cleared the right-centre field wall. It was Worrell's third blown save in 13 opportunities.
Eric Karros had an RBI double and a solo homer for the Dodgers.

In Philadelphia, Gregg Jefferies broke a tie with a two-out, two-run double in the eighth and Curt Schilling pitched a four-hitter as the Phillies won their third straight game, 3-1 over the Colorado Rockies.
Schilling (5-3) walked none and recorded 12 strikeouts for the fourth time in his career.
The Phillies, who can sweep the four-game set with a win Monday, sent Colorado to a season-high fifth straight loss.
Rico Brogna extended his hitting streak to 14 games when he doubled to start the seventh against John Thomson (0-1), who was making his major-league debut.
In San Diego, Archi Cianfrocco's single off Jeff Brantley scored Derek Lee from second base with none out in the 11th and lifted the Padres to a 5-4 win over the Cincinnati Reds.
Trevor Hoffman (1-2) pitched two hitless innings to earn the win. Mike Remlinger (0-2) took the loss.
